title: What's new
lead: What changed in Tavvit, newest first.

1.41.3.title: New badges, nicer tags, sound for everyone

items.badges: Badges have new pictures. Beside a name they stand together in one strip, and a click on one opens a small card with its name, what it means and the kind of badge it is.
items.tags: Space tags are made anew: the space's colour as a small seal with its symbol, the letters beside it on a plain plate that stays readable on any card.
items.dates: Messages from three or more days ago show their date beside the time, so an old conversation says when it happened without scrolling up to its day.
items.watch: Watching together: if someone else pressed play and you heard nothing, you now get the sound, or a button that starts it with one click. A video that plays muted is caught the same way.
items.output: YouTube and Vimeo play on your system's default output. If your calls use another device, you are told once, so a silent video is no mystery.
items.overlay: The mark of a voice channel's OBS overlay no longer lies under its settings button.

items.theme: Your profile theme now has a strength: soft as before, strong for the whole card in your colours, or whole card with your colours bright around the text. Settings, Account, under the colours.
items.portal: The developer portal is new: your bots down the side, and each one with its profile, token, invite, commands and spaces in tabs.
items.botProfile: Bots can have a banner and a username of their own instead of bot-and-a-number. A change to a bot's name or pictures shows to everyone at once.
items.notFriends: Bots can't be added as friends or messaged, and their cards no longer offer it. Trying with a bot's name says so plainly.

items.voice: Fixed: someone whose connection stuttered for a moment (a tab in the background, a phone switching apps, a short network drop) no longer left the voice channel for everyone else a minute later while still talking, and watching together no longer asked them to join a call they were in.
items.watch: After such a moment, the video you watch together catches up with anything that changed meanwhile.
items.preview: Fixed: deleting or editing the last message of a conversation now changes its preview in every list at once, instead of still showing what was deleted.
items.phone: On the phone, hold a conversation with one person to close it, as on the desktop. Leaving a group there now asks first.
items.errors: If closing a conversation or leaving a group does not work, you are told why.

items.studio: A new theme studio shapes how the app looks with a live preview: the colours, the accent, the light, the corners, the typeface, the shape of pictures and how messages are drawn and spaced. Open it from Settings, Appearance.
items.looks: Keep the looks you like under a name and switch between them with one click, up to 30 on each device.
items.share: Share a look as a link. The whole look is in the link, so nothing is stored anywhere, and whoever opens it sees it first and puts it on with one click.
items.spaces: A space can choose its own colours in Space settings, Look. Members see them while they are in the space; turn this off in Settings, Appearance, Spaces in their own colours.
items.yours: Contrast, text size, motion, status colours, underlined links, the clock and the sidebar's width are never part of a look: they stay as you set them.
items.audit: Changing a space's tag or colours now shows in its audit log.

items.post: A link to a post on Bluesky shows the post: who wrote it, its text with its links, its pictures, video or link, the post it quotes, and its replies, reposts and likes.
items.video: Videos from Bluesky play right in the chat with their own controls: play and pause, a timeline, sound, picture in picture and full screen. Bluesky's GIFs loop without sound.
items.viewer: Pictures open in a new viewer: several in a row with a strip to move between them, zoom by button, wheel or double click, and open, copy, save, reply or forward from there. Uploaded pictures open in it too.
items.privacy: Pictures and videos from Bluesky load only after you agree, like every other preview. Posts Bluesky marks as sensitive stay covered until you choose to see them.

items.dot: While someone is live on Twitch, their status dot turns purple with a play mark, in the member list, your DMs, friends and their profile. Their status and notifications stay as they are.

items.message: Administrators can remove a message in a space straight from its menu, without waiting for a report.
items.parts: In the admin console they can remove parts of a profile, such as the picture, the name, About me, the status, links or decorations, and parts of a space, such as its icon, banner, description or tag.
items.space: They can remove a space's emoji, stickers and sounds one by one, or delete a whole space.
items.told: Each time, the person it concerns is told in their own language what was removed, why and how to object, and the administrators' log keeps it. Direct messages stay private: administrators act on one only when someone reports it.
items.deleted: Fixed: a deleted space stayed in its members' list until they reloaded the page.

items.scroll: Scrolling through a channel and through long member lists is smooth again, also with many decorated people in them.
items.switch: Switching between channels and spaces is faster: a channel you left at its newest message comes back at once.
items.motion: Decorations and animated profile pictures in lists and chats stand still until you point at someone, and move as before on a profile.
items.stuck: Fixed: after switching spaces, the channel list and the member list could stay loading for good.

items.make: Make your own decorations: a frame or a nameplate from a picture you upload (PNG, WebP or GIF, moving or still), an effect from one small piece that moves across your profile the way you choose (falling, tumbling, rising, floating or twinkling), and a name style from a look and your colours.
items.share: Share them in your server's community gallery, sorted by popular or new and searchable by name, where everyone can wear them with one click. Each shows who made it and how many wear it.
items.safe: Nothing you make can cover a profile: a frame keeps clear of the picture, an effect's pieces are small and few, and a nameplate fades out before the name.
items.report: Anyone can report a design, and administrators can remove one with a reason its maker is told. A removed design disappears from everyone who wore it at once.

items.drawn: Every frame, profile effect and nameplate is now a drawing: headphones, cat ears, a crown, an angel's halo and wings, horns, a laurel wreath, flowers, flames, snow, stars, hearts and bubbles round your picture; a record, a city, cherry blossoms, snowy pines, a rain cloud, a campfire, a starry night, a boat at sea, mountains, a forest and bunting at the end of your row.
items.effects: Profile effects now play across your whole card: butterflies, music, a night sky, snow, cherry blossoms, autumn leaves, hearts, confetti, bubbles and lanterns.
items.names: Ten new name effects: Wave, Glitch, Sticker, Comic, Retro, Candy cane, Galaxy, Toxic, Lagoon and Berry.
items.kept: If you wore one of the earlier designs, you now wear the drawing closest to it. Nothing to do.

items.tags: Spaces can have a tag: two to four letters with a symbol and a colour. Members wear it beside their name, and a click on it shows the space. Set it in Space settings → Tag, wear it in Your settings.
items.overlay: Show a voice channel in your stream: right-click it, Overlay for OBS, and add the link as a browser source. It shows who is there and who is speaking, and everyone in the channel sees that it can be shown.
items.page: A new page at /creators says what Tavvit offers a community and how to move in.

items.look: Badges have a new look: matte metal marks, a little larger, and without the glow, on profiles, on spaces and on a badge's card.

items.decorations: Decorate your profile in Settings → Decorations: a frame for your picture, an effect over your banner, a nameplate in member lists, and a typeface and an effect for your name. Free for everyone, and tried on in a preview before you save.
items.where: They show on your profile card, in member lists, in your DMs and beside your messages, and move while someone points at you. Where a role gives your name its colour, the colour stays and only the typeface changes.

items.linked: Link your Twitch account in Settings → Linked accounts by signing in at Twitch, so only your own can be linked. Your profile shows it, and while you're live people see it, with a button to your stream. A Twitch link among your profile links no longer does that.

items.backgrounds: Your camera can blur your room, softly or strongly, or put you in one of five scenes, among them a tavern, or in front of a picture of your own. It all happens on your device, and your picture never leaves it.
items.streamer: Streamer mode hides your email, invite links, connected instances, two-factor codes, session addresses, tokens and what notifications say while you stream. Turn it on in Settings → Privacy or with a shortcut; the desktop app turns it on by itself when OBS, Streamlabs or XSplit starts.
items.twitch: Link your Twitch channel on your profile, and people see when you're live, like a game you're playing, with a button to your stream. The server's operator turns this on.
items.subtitles: Watching together no longer turns subtitles on by itself. A new button turns them on for you alone.
items.profile: Your own profile no longer lists friends and spaces in common with yourself.

items.stage: The product page now opens on Night Shift, a demo space to walk through: its channels drawn as a floor plan, and every room to try, from writing in #general and joining the lounge to voting in a poll and watching along at movie night.
items.rules: The way in shows how a space greets new people: its welcome, its rules, and what opens once you agree to them.
items.window: The space's member list, with everyone under their role, and the seven looks are right there in its window.

1.34.1.title: A proper card for shared links

items.preview: A link to Tavvit now shows a proper card in chats and on social sites: the logo, what Tavvit is and a look at the app.
items.pages: The product page and the Help, Status, Roadmap and What's new pages arrive ready to read before any script has loaded, so they open faster and search engines can read them.
items.icon: Browser tabs, bookmarks and search results show Tavvit's icon at every size.

items.spaceEmoji: Every space can have its own emoji, up to 200, and stickers, up to 60. Everyone can use them in the space's channels, and its members anywhere on the server.
items.import: Space settings, Get from Discord brings a Discord server's emoji and stickers over with a bot of your own. Its token is used for two requests to Discord and never stored.
items.announce: A ready-made announcement in five languages tells your Discord server where you went, and its link welcomes everyone who follows.
items.pickers: The emoji and sticker pickers show the space you are writing in first, then the server's emoji, then your other spaces.
items.right: A new right, Manage Emoji and Stickers, decides who may add, rename and remove them.
items.elsewhere: Emoji in a space on another server now show there, and reactions with them work.

1.33.2.title: A new product page, banners and tooltips

items.landing: The product page is new. It reads like a space: its chapters stand in a column of their own and turn read as you go, Ctrl K jumps between them, and pointing at the app's window lights the part it names.
items.banners: A space's banner now heads its channel list, on the desktop and on the phone, and its card on Home.
items.home: Your spaces come first on Home, as large cards with their banner, what is new in them and who is talking.
items.sidebar: Explore and About fold under More in Home's column, and a space has one Create row for channels and categories.
items.tooltips: Every button that shows only an icon names itself as soon as the pointer rests on it or the keyboard reaches it.
items.search: Home has no second search field any more: the one in the top bar opens the same.

1.33.1.title: Deleting an account that owns spaces

items.admin: Administrators can delete an account together with the spaces it owns, for a name nobody should carry or an account made for spam. Each space goes on the record.

items.watch: Watch a YouTube or Vimeo video or a video file together in a voice channel. Everyone sees the same moment, and anyone in the call can pause, skip or add to the queue.
items.steer: Whoever starts can choose to steer alone, and the video gets quieter while someone speaks.
items.reactions: Reactions rise over the picture, and the channel list shows what a voice channel is watching.
items.privacy: A video from YouTube or Vimeo loads on your device only after your yes, and nothing of what you watch is stored.

1.32.8.title: Safer accounts, calls and links between servers

items.accounts: A new account that still has to confirm its address can only read in spaces until it has, and throwaway addresses can be refused at sign-up.
items.privacy: Banners and the icons of groups and spaces from other servers wait for your yes too, and the privacy notice says plainly that messages are not end-to-end encrypted.
items.voice: Muting or deafening someone in a voice channel now holds even when their app ignores it.
items.limits: Sounds, group pictures and files from bots count towards the storage an account may use, and an account can be in at most 100 groups.
items.signin: Guessing passwords is slowed down everywhere a password is asked for, without keeping you out of your own account.
items.desktop: The desktop app only listens for shortcuts that cannot type text, on any keyboard layout.
items.federation: Between servers, a server has to prove its address before it is trusted, and nobody is put into a group, chat, call or friend request here that they would not accept.

items.privacy: Pictures and invites from other servers wait for your yes before they load, in invite cards, in Outer Space and on links to an invite elsewhere too.
items.limits: The server refuses oversized requests before it reads them, and no account can fill its disk by forwarding or uploading over and over.
items.moderation: Someone kicked or banned is out of the space's voice and news at once and can no longer edit old messages. Taking a channel out of a private category takes the right to manage roles.
items.previews: Link previews and media files can no longer be turned against the server's own network.
items.federation: Between servers, only those taking part may answer or end a call, and an account can no longer claim someone else's identity.

items.start: 1.32.5 did not start on servers that send mail through Resend. 1.32.6 does, and every version is now started that way once before it ships.

items.files: Files sent before the last update also get addresses nobody can guess, over the next days.
items.shortcuts: Shortcuts in the desktop app need Ctrl, Alt or the system key for letters, digits and Space, so the app never hears what you type in other programs.
items.server: Under the hood, the server runs on a newer framework, with stricter checks on where a request comes from.

items.media: Stickers, profile pictures and icons only come from this server or from the server a person lives on. A sticker from anywhere else waits until you choose to load it.
items.voice: A private voice channel stays private: nobody who cannot see it can join it or see who is in it.
items.files: Uploaded files get addresses nobody can guess.

items.icons: A space can give each channel its own icon, one of the set or an emoji, in place of the channel type icon.

items.username: You can now change your username in your account settings, once in 30 days.
items.roadmap: The roadmap shows what comes next.

items.translate: Right-click a message, or hold it on a phone, and choose Translate. The translation stands under the original, and you choose the language in your settings.

1.32.0.title: Forums, announcements and an address of your own

items.forums: A forum channel keeps questions and topics apart as posts: each has a title, tags and its own conversation, and the list follows what is going on.
items.announcements: An announcement channel is written by a few and read by everyone. Other spaces can follow it, and each post then also arrives in their channel.
items.address: A space can have an invite address in words, such as /join/night-shift, that never runs out.

1.31.0.title: Much faster when many people are here

items.speed: Messages arrive quickly even with a thousand people online, and starting the app takes far less data.
items.pages: This page is new, and so are a help page and a status page.
items.safety: A signed-out or suspended account is put out of a voice call at once.

items.docs: Everything about bots and webhooks, with a quickstart, at /developers.

items.cards: Bots can show cards with titles, fields and pictures.
items.commands: Slash commands can ask for things, and answer you alone.
items.portal: A page of your own for your bots: picture, token, invite address.

items.storage: See how much room your files take up under Settings, Account.

items.games: The desktop app asks Steam, Epic and GOG directly which game you are playing.

items.bots: Bots can join spaces, with slash commands, under the rights a space gives them.

items.voice: Record a voice message right in the chat.
items.saved: Save messages, and be reminded of them.
items.alerts: Get alerted when someone writes a word you choose.
items.soundboard: Play clips to everyone in a call with the soundboard.

items.threads: Follow a side conversation in a thread of its own.
items.events: Plan events in a space, with reminders.
items.welcome: Spaces can welcome new members and ask them to accept the rules.

1.23.0.title: More you can do with a message

items.pins: Pin messages, hide spoilers, forward, and hold polls.
items.push: Get notifications while the app is closed.
